transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-10-29 15:00 UTC
Duration: 56 minutes
Attendees: Sofia (Redwood AE), Ethan (Redwood SE), Maya (Redwood CSM), Priya (NimbleHealth Head of Platform), Mark (SRE), Anika (CTO), Samir (Eng Manager)

Summary:
Short check-in focused on surge/readiness concerns around the upcoming product analytics release (expected traffic spike during monthly batch), discussion of dedicated vs hosted burst strategies, cost tradeoffs, and concrete pilot commitments for a 3-day stress test and canary rollout.

Topics: surge readiness, autoscaling, KV cache pre-warm, dedicated burst capacity, SOC2/KMS questions, pilot SOW and pricing

[00:00:03] Sofia (Redwood): ok everybody thanks for joining, um we'll keep this focused, we have about 55 minutes, looks like Priya, is that right on your side for timing?
[00:00:10] Priya (NimbleHealth): yeah that's right, thanks. We wanted this to be practical — our release in mid-November has a recurring weekly batch that causes a 6-8x spike for about 6 hours, and last time our p95 latency went from 120ms to 800ms so we need to avoid that.
[00:00:28] Ethan (Redwood): thanks for the context, that helps a lot. Quick clarifying Q: is most of that traffic syncs/embeds or generation?
[00:00:34] Mark (NimbleHealth): it's mixed, primarily generation for report summaries plus some embedding refreshes. The big cost is the generation tokens, and then some heavy KV cache churn because of many long contexts.
[00:00:44] Ethan (Redwood): okay, so two levers — batching + pre-warm KV, and then routing to burst capacity. We discussed earlier dedicated reserved capacity vs hosted with burst. Wanted to outline tradeoffs again.
[00:00:56] Anika (NimbleHealth): cost is important but also SLA — if we get timeouts customers complain. We prefer a hosted route if performance matches, but we need predictable p95 during spike windows.
[00:01:08] Sofia (Redwood): understood. For predictability, dedicated capacity with reserved nodes gives the best consistent p95 but costs more. Hosted with burst is cheaper overall but you rely on our capacity pool and fallback routing. We can simulate both with the pilot.
[00:01:21] Samir (NimbleHealth): curious what the fallback looks like — if the model variant isn't available, do you degrade gracefully?
[00:01:27] Ethan (Redwood): yes — we can route to a slightly smaller quantized variant automatically; responses are livelier but maybe less precise. We also support autoscaling policies that pre-provision burst capacity for known windows. There's a config we call 'predictive burst' that pre-warms topology.
[00:01:44] Priya (NimbleHealth): 'predictive burst' — is that the one that does pre-warm KV caches? Last time we saw cold KV cache miss spikes.
[00:01:51] Ethan (Redwood): right, we have KV pre-warm where we prime the most common prefixes; it's part of the pre-warm plan. Note: pre-warming increases short-term cost because you're holding KV and warmed GPUs but reduces tail latency.
[00:02:05] Priya: okay. We need numbers to decide. Give us an estimate of cost delta for 6-hour window.
[00:02:11] Sofia: we can do that — Ethan will run a stress test with representative traffic and then produce a delta: hosted baseline vs hosted with predictive burst vs dedicated reserved. That will be in the stress test report.
[00:02:21] Mark: also SOC2 logs — we need the detailed audit log sample for compliance review. Last quarter we escalated this.
[00:02:27] Maya (Redwood): we have the recent SOC2 artifact and audit log schema; we'll share the sample logs and KMS integration doc in the follow-up.
[00:02:36] Anika: what about data residency? Some data can't leave the EU region. Can we pin the serving region?
[00:02:42] Ethan: yes, we can pin routing to eu-west-1, and for Private deployments we support VPC/private control plane. For hosted burst, bursts are region-aware; we'll guarantee the serving region as long as capacity is available, otherwise we trigger an alert and a fallback to your dedicated nodes or to on-prem if part of Private setup.
[00:03:01] Priya: okay good.

[00:03:10] (30 second marker — brief cross talk about calendars)

[00:03:40] Samir: technical deep dive — when you say quantized variant, what's the perf delta? p50/p95 numbers?
[00:03:46] Ethan: rough numbers — full FP16 variant: p95 under 200ms on our c5-like instances for these models, 8-bit quantized can add 20–40ms at p50 but varies with sequence length; p95 can drift up during heavy KV churn. We'll include actual model profiles in the report. Also note sequence length distribution matters a lot.
[00:04:05] Mark: our sequences can be long — many reports are 2.5k tokens average, sometimes 4k. Does your runtime support variable chunking? We've hit OOM with long contexts before.
[00:04:12] Ethan: yes — we have chunked attention and dynamic kv eviction policies. For very long contexts we recommend our streaming tokenization + chunked prompts to reduce peak memory and use KV caching aggressively. We'll propose a memory/eviction policy for your workload.
[00:04:29] Priya: please add that to the pilot config.

[00:04:40] (murmurs)

[00:04:55] Sofia: on the pilot scope — propose a 3-day window that mirrors your monthly spike pattern: day 1 baseline small traffic, day 2 repeat spike in hosted baseline, day 3 run hosted with predictive burst and dedicated reserved nodes for comparison. We'll capture latency distributions, cost run rate, error rates, and failover behavior.
[00:05:13] Priya: sounds good. Are we allowed to share synthetic traffic or do you need real samples?
[00:05:18] Ethan: synthetic is fine if it's representative. Ideally you give us a p95/p99 target and a sample list of payloads, but we can take a sanitized anonymized trace.
[00:05:28] Mark: we'll provide a 24-hour sample of representative traffic and the expected spike waveform.

[00:05:40] Maya: I'll coordinate calendar invites and make sure legal gets the pilot SOW template.

[00:05:49] (short silence)

[00:06:00] Priya: a couple of other items — error budgets and alerts. We want a playbook when p95 breaches 400ms during the spike. What's your recommended guardrail?
[00:06:10] Ethan: our standard is an autoscaling policy plus canary fallback: if p95 > threshold for 2 consecutive 5-min windows, trigger pre-warm + route to reserved, and notify on-call. We'll give you the alert thresholds and runbook. You can also configure soft-fallback to smaller model variants to keep tail latencies bounded.
[00:06:27] Samir: do we get token-level cost breakdown per route? We need it for product economics.
[00:06:33] Maya: yes, Redwood Console provides token-level and per-route cost attribution; we'll include a quickstart to wire up your product routes into the console.

[00:06:45] (Ethan explains a bit of architecture)

[00:07:10] Ethan: a quick note on KV terminology — sorry sometimes transcripts say KV cash, that's the speech-to-text glitch — it's KV cache. For pre-warming we use prefix frequency analysis.
[00:07:19] Mark: noted.

[00:07:30] Priya: security question — we need to ensure keys live in our KMS; how does the integration look?
[00:07:35] Sofia: we support customer-managed keys via standard KMS integrations (AWS KMS, GCP KMS) and on private deployments HSM. We'll send the integration guide.

[00:07:48] Anika: what SLA can we expect if we go with reserved nodes?
[00:07:52] Maya: reserved/dedicated comes with a higher SLA (99.9% uptime) and guaranteed throughput per node. Hosted best-effort pool is lower; we'll share exact numbers in the pricing doc.

[00:08:05] (short interruption — someone muted/unmuted)

[00:08:20] Sofia: let's capture concrete deliverables: 1) stress test run and report, 2) pricing comparison for the 6-hour spike using your sample, 3) pilot SOW for the 3-day run, including region pinning and KMS notes, 4) a canary rollout plan and runbook.
[00:08:35] Priya: ok those are the right items. For the stress test, can you simulate our exact concurrency pattern? We have bursts every 5 minutes during ramp windows.
[00:08:43] Ethan: yes, we can model the waveform and run multiple iterations to get confidence intervals. We'll include p50/p95/p99 and error breakdowns.

[00:08:55] Mark: also we want an ingress throttling suggestion so our producer side doesn't overwhelm the network.
[00:08:59] Ethan: we'll propose a token-bucket throttle per route and a graceful reconnect backoff pattern.

[00:09:10] Priya: test data — we will scrub PHI and share a sanitized trace. Legal will need the SOW but it's standard.

[00:09:20] Maya: I'll put legal and security docs in the follow-up package.

[00:09:30] (15 min mark — high level recap and small tangent about holiday schedules)

[00:09:55] (longer technical exchange between Ethan and Mark about eviction policy — transcript has a few overlaps and mis-ids)
[00:20:05] Ethan: so for eviction, we recommend LRU with TTL on prefixes, and an active prefetch list for the top-k prefixes, that way cold tails don't blow up the KV cache. We'll include a suggested policy tuned for 2.5k average sequences.
[00:20:20] Mark: LRU + TTL makes sense, just need numbers.

[00:20:30] (cross talk, someone says 'uh-huh')

[00:21:05] Sofia: pricing — two quick options: a reserved baseline (monthly commit) sized to your 2x normal + a burst bucket for the extra 6-hour spike, or hosted with predictive burst where you pay a small prep fee plus usage. We'll quantify this in the pricing sheet.
[00:21:25] Priya: our finance will prefer the burst model if the delta isn't huge.

[00:21:35] Anika: also want to know rollback time for canary if something goes sideways.
[00:21:40] Ethan: typical rollback is under 3 minutes if autoscaling isn't yet triggered; with pre-warm actions it could take longer to drain but we have health-check based immediate routing back to old variant. We'll detail timing in the runbook.

[00:21:55] (small pause)

[00:22:10] Sofia: ok moving to timeline — we propose: Oct 30 receive traffic sample & targets, Nov 2 stress harness ready, Nov 3 pilot kickoff, Nov 9 pilot completed with report. Does that work?
[00:22:23] Priya: Nov 3 kickoff is tight but doable. We can aim for that.

[00:22:30] Samir: can we add a quick P0 checklist for the on-call person? We want to make sure ops knows steps.
[00:22:36] Maya: yes will include P0 checklist in the runbook.

[00:22:45] (small logistics talk)

[00:22:55] (someone shares a link in chat — 'pilot-sow-v1.pdf')

[00:23:10] Priya: last technical Q — is there a transparent way to see token consumption per request in real time? That's required for our billing reconciliation.
[00:23:18] Maya: yes, the console streams per-request token metrics and you can pipe them into your internal BI. We'll give you a dashboard template.

[00:23:30] (40 minute mark — summary)

[00:23:45] Sofia: recap — action list: Ethan runs stress test and preps harness; Sofia sends pricing & SOW; Maya pushes legal/security docs and schedules the Nov 3 kickoff; NimbleHealth provides scrubbed sample and acceptance criteria. We'll aim to have the stress test by Nov 2.

[00:24:05] Priya: perfect, thank you — excited to validate.

[00:24:12] (brief friendly sign-off, some goodbyes)
